anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads the report as a CSV file, reading rows in pages of at most 100 with a 4-second deadline and returning "not found" for unknown reports. It covers the button and the bounded export. As the spec intends, it exports the 12 columns shown by default rather than all 40, because the full table is too wide for most readers. It defers emailed exports and audit-log events to acme/widgets#46, and the under-5-seconds target on production data is checked after merge.

Nothing blocks merging. The checks passed in CI on the commit being reviewed. The tests cover the exact column list and order, escaping of commas, quotes and line breaks in cells, the paging limit, the deadline, and the response for unknown reports. One smaller point does not block merging: the export pages through rows with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper in lib/page.ts, so any later change to paging rules would have to be made in two places. The fix nits option can take that change. You are the author, so approval is not offered because you cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because nothing blocks it and the checks passed.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR at the commit being reviewed. [recommended]
2. fix nits - switch the export to the shared paging helper, review and push that change, watch the checks once, then return here.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the worktree and branch as they are.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After drops the Delivers label and the AC row numbers and names the covered, deviated and deferred behaviors plainly with the acme/widgets#46 reference intact, which is the right direction, but the opening runs four sentences (adds button/paging; covers the button; exports 12 of 40 per spec; defers email/audit plus the post-merge check), so it does not satisfy f1's two-sentence requirement. It also invents a rationale ("the full table is too wide for most readers") that the spec does not state; use the spec's own reason. A wording that keeps every fact and delivers the Change: "This PR adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads the report in pages of at most 100 rows under a 4-second deadline, returning not-found for unknown reports, and as the spec intends it exports the 12 columns shown by default rather than all 40. Emailed exports and audit-log events are deferred to acme/widgets#46, and the under-5-seconds target on production data is checked after merge rather than here." Keep the test and nit detail in the following gate paragraph and the AC-to-row mapping under show evidence, as After already does.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change: the opening is two plain sentences naming behaviors (on-demand CSV downloads with bounded paging, the deliberate 12-column choice, email delivery and audit events deferred to acme/widgets#46, production timing checked after merge) with no row numbers and no Delivers label, so f1 moves from fails to holds, while the gate still lists zero blockers, merge is offered, no blocker is minted for the deferred or deviating rows, and nothing is posted without a pick. One wording risk: the first sentence says 'on-demand CSV downloads' rather than naming the Export CSV button, so a stricter reader could argue the button itself is not described as covered; writing 'adds an Export CSV button that downloads a CSV with bounded paging, a 4-second deadline, and a 404 for unknown reports' would name the UI mechanism explicitly without reintroducing row numbers. Also note the evidence summary (CI test success, 0 binding pending checks, merge_state_status CLEAN) now lives only behind show evidence; that is consistent with the Change, but keep the hint line's parenthetical if you want the gate verdict to remain self-evidencing in the main body.
